# Code Review Report — PR #240
**Branch:** feat/issue-230-migrate-reviewer-family
**Reviewer:** Claude (Reviewer mode)
**Date:** 2026-04-29
**Commit:** a08bf57 feat(agents): migrate Reviewer family to OpenCode (#230)

---

## Review Summary

This PR adds five new `.opencode/agents/*.md` agent definition files — three model-specific reviewer sub-agents (Kimi, Qwen, GLM), one synthesizing reviewer, and one standalone PR reviewer — migrating the Reviewer family from the Copilot `.github/agents-openrouter/` format to OpenCode's `.opencode/agents/` format. No production code is changed; all changes are agent instruction files.

The core concern is a probable name-derivation mismatch: OpenCode derives agent dispatch names from filenames (pattern confirmed by `test-writer.md` → "Test Writer"), but three of the new files use hyphenated model-abbreviation filenames (`reviewer-glm.md`, `reviewer-kimi.md`, `reviewer-qwen.md`) that yield names like "Reviewer Glm" rather than the parenthetical forms ("Reviewer (GLM)", etc.) expected by the orchestrator's `permission.task.allow` list. If this derivation holds, the orchestrator's Step 7 review cycle cannot dispatch these agents.

**Files Reviewed:** 5
**Findings:** 1 Critical, 1 Warning, 2 Suggestions

---

## Findings

### Critical Findings

```
[C-01] Agent filename-derived names don't match orchestrator dispatch names
Category: Correctness
Severity: Critical
File: .opencode/agents/reviewer-glm.md, .opencode/agents/reviewer-kimi.md, .opencode/agents/reviewer-qwen.md
Lines: 1–3 (frontmatter)
Description: OpenCode derives an agent's dispatch name from its filename stem using
hyphen-to-space conversion and title-casing — confirmed by the existing working agent
`test-writer.md` which is dispatched as "Test Writer". Applied consistently:

  reviewer-glm.md  → "Reviewer Glm"   (orchestrator expects "Reviewer (GLM)")
  reviewer-kimi.md → "Reviewer Kimi"  (orchestrator expects "Reviewer (Kimi)")
  reviewer-qwen.md → "Reviewer Qwen"  (orchestrator expects "Reviewer (Qwen)")

None of the new files contain a `name:` YAML frontmatter field (none of the existing
OpenCode agents do either). The orchestrator's `permission.task.allow` list
(orchestrator-v3.md lines 41–43) and Phase B dispatch instructions (line 553–555) both
reference the parenthetical forms. OpenCode dispatch is name-gated: if the runtime name
does not match the allow-list entry, dispatch is blocked or requires manual confirmation.
All three reviewer sub-agent dispatches in Step 7 would fail silently or require user
intervention, effectively preventing the automated review cycle from running.

Suggestion: Verify OpenCode's exact naming convention by inspecting the opencode-rules
documentation or running a test dispatch. If OpenCode does NOT support a `name:` field
and does use filename derivation, rename the files:
  reviewer-glm.md  → a filename that OpenCode resolves to "Reviewer (GLM)"
or update the orchestrator allow-list to use the filename-derived names:
  "Reviewer (GLM)" → "Reviewer Glm"
  "Reviewer (Kimi)" → "Reviewer Kimi"
  "Reviewer (Qwen)" → "Reviewer Qwen"
If OpenCode DOES support a `name:` field in agent frontmatter, add it to each file:
  name: "Reviewer (GLM)"
and update the other new agents accordingly. The `synthesizing-reviewer.md` file
is unaffected — its filename yields "Synthesizing Reviewer" which matches the
orchestrator allow-list exactly.
```

---

### Warning Findings

```
[W-01] pr-reviewer.md description contradicts orchestrator allow-list placement
Category: Documentation
Severity: Warning
File: .opencode/agents/pr-reviewer.md
Lines: 30
Description: The body text states: "You are **not** part of the Orchestrator workflow
— the Orchestrator uses the Synthesizing Reviewer for local code reviews instead."
However, "PR Reviewer" is explicitly listed in `orchestrator-v3.md`'s
`permission.task.allow` (line 45). The statement is not factually wrong (the PR Reviewer
is not used in the standard Step 7 cycle), but it is misleading: the orchestrator CAN
dispatch the PR Reviewer for ad-hoc GitHub PR reviews. An agent reading this description
may incorrectly conclude it will never be called from the Orchestrator.

Additionally, if OpenCode applies the same filename-derivation rule described in C-01,
`pr-reviewer.md` → "Pr Reviewer", which does not match "PR Reviewer" in the
allow-list (the all-caps "PR" abbreviation is lost). This secondary concern depends on
whether OpenCode special-cases abbreviation casing; it should be verified alongside C-01.

Suggestion: Revise the description to: "You are not part of the Step 7 Synthesized
Local Review cycle — that cycle uses the three model-specific reviewer sub-agents and
the Synthesizing Reviewer. You are dispatched by the Orchestrator or invoked directly
by the user for ad-hoc GitHub PR reviews." Verify the dispatch name issue in tandem
with C-01 resolution.
```

```
[S-02] synthesizing-reviewer.md: Step 5 output path uses implicit YYYY-MM-DD format with no formatting note
Category: Documentation
Severity: Suggestion
File: .opencode/agents/synthesizing-reviewer.md
Lines: ~213 (Step 5)
Description: Step 5 instructs the agent to write to
`.github/notes/reviews/YYYY-MM-DD-pr{N}-synthesis.md`. This matches the orchestrator's
Phase C dispatch prompt. However, the variable `{N}` is not defined in the
Synthesizing Reviewer's own file — its value arrives implicitly through the dispatch
prompt context. An agent reading this instruction without seeing the dispatch prompt
may not know how to populate `{N}`. The orchestrator's Phase C prompt does include the
PR number, so this works in practice, but a brief note ("N = PR number, provided in
the dispatch prompt") would make the contract explicit.

Note: Low impact. The agent receives the PR number in context. Minor clarity improvement.
```

## Overall Assessment

The PR is structurally sound: five well-formed OpenCode agent files, correct permission models, consistent `mode: subagent` declarations, appropriate bash allow-lists, and body text that correctly references existing shared process files (`_shared/code-review-process.md`, `_shared/communication.md`, `_shared/multi-model-synthesis.md`, `_shared/pr-review-process.md`, `_shared/local-workflow.md`, `_shared/repo-context.md` — all confirmed to exist on disk). Commit message follows convention, branch name follows convention, scope is appropriate.

The blocking concern is C-01: the filename-to-dispatch-name derivation that OpenCode uses almost certainly does not produce parenthetical names like "Reviewer (GLM)" from `reviewer-glm.md`. If the derivation rule is hyphen-to-space + title-case (as demonstrated by the existing `test-writer.md` → "Test Writer"), then the three model-specific reviewer agents will not be dispatched correctly by the orchestrator's Step 7, making the review cycle non-functional. This must be verified and resolved before merge. The `synthesizing-reviewer.md` agent is not affected — its filename derives to "Synthesizing Reviewer" which matches the orchestrator allow-list.

**Not ready to merge until C-01 is resolved.** All other changes are acceptable.
